old_findings.note: Only the display is fixed: the data slot now shows whole bytes (0x036b...). It is still the folded keccak constant instead of sha3(5)/sha3(6), the allocation size 'floor32(_3 - 97) + 128' and the copy while loops remain.

improvements: exit(): the via-IR internal-function-pointer temporaries are resolved. stor[mem[_108 + 32]] now prints as stor7, the 'mem[_108] != 3: Panic(81)' check on a value just written is dropped (exact), and the dead struct writes (mem[_108] = 3 / 7, zero inits) are gone. The pointer bumps are folded into the allocation checks' cumulative offsets (mem[64] + 128 / 192 / 256), which are equivalent; later code only uses decoded calls and scratch memory.
notes: Diff of 46 lines, read in full (name: display only; exit: function-pointer resolution). Calls, events and storage writes are unchanged; one dominated Panic(81) check removed.
summary: No regression. exit() loses its via-IR function-pointer noise (slot resolved to stor7), and name()'s slot constant shows whole bytes.
